product.name: Evolve Loop
product.oneBreath: Your AI writes the code. A second AI reviews it. A dependable process, not an opinion, decides if it ships.

hero.headlineLead: Ship the code your agent wrote —
hero.subhead: Evolve Loop puts your AI coder in a structured pipeline that repairs itself. The pipeline plans the work, and an independent reviewer challenges it. Only safe changes merge, and each run makes the next run better. A code change ships only after a test failed first, unless the change is trivial.

problem.heading: Agents can write the feature now. The hard part is the merge.
body: AI can write a feature, fix a bug or refactor a module without help. The code is not the bottleneck now. The bottleneck is trust: can you merge the code without a read of every line?
Most tools stop at "an AI wrote it." The hard part comes after: is it the right change, is it correct, and will it break something downstream?

theTurn.heading: Intelligence proposes. A dependable process decides.
body: AI is strong at three decisions: what to build, how to build it and what looks wrong. The pipeline lets AI make these decisions freely.
A structured, repeatable process decides what is safe to ship. Its guardrails are code, and the AI cannot argue with code. Freedom where it helps, structure where it counts.

phaseSpine.blurb: It changes a vague request into a clear goal, and it names the risky assumptions first.
It examines the code and the past lessons. Then it proposes the work that is worth the effort.
It decides what this cycle does and what waits, so the scope stays small.
It makes the change in isolation, after a test that fails first. Then the builder simplifies and reviews its own diff.
By default, a reviewer from a different model family challenges the work and decides if it holds up. Before it, a code review scores the change on ten dimensions, in shadow.
It merges only the work that passed, with a record of each step.
It turns the result into a permanent lesson for the next cycle.

pipelineDemo.heading: The model composes its own pipeline.
pipelineDemo.sub: Give it a goal. The advisor runs the mandated phases, picks from the common phases and writes new phases when the goal needs them. Then one routing table gives each phase that uses a model its CLI and model. agy runs first, on Gemini 3.8 Flash High. At the deep and top tiers, Claude Opus runs through agy first and through Claude Code second. Nothing here is pre-scripted.
pipelineDemo.routeNote: One routing table gives each phase that uses a model its CLI and model. Below the deep tier, agy runs first, on Gemini 3.8 Flash High. The auditor, the tdd engineer and the code reviewer run on Claude Code only. Thus by default, the build and the review use different model families. Ship is host code, and it uses no model.

pillarsIntro.heading: Designed like a team, not a one-shot prompt.

pillars.title: AI-driven, end to end
pillars.claim: It designs the work. It does not only type it.
pillars.proof: The pipeline decides what to build, how to approach it and what is risky. It applies real judgment at every step, not one prompt into the dark.

pillars.title: A pipeline that adapts
pillars.claim: Structure that changes shape for the task.
pillars.proof: Every change follows the same clear pipeline, but the pipeline flexes. A one-line fix skips the ceremony, and a risky feature gets more review. The pipeline is structured enough to trust and dynamic enough to stay fast.

pillars.title: Agile by nature
pillars.claim: Plan, build, review, reflect: every cycle.
pillars.proof: Each cycle runs like a sprint: scope the work, build it, review it, ship it, then learn. The scope stays bounded, so nothing sprawls and the progress compounds.

pillars.title: Self-repair
pillars.claim: A failure does not stop it. A failure teaches it.
pillars.proof: When something breaks, the pipeline catches it, recovers and turns the failure into a permanent rule. If only audit gates forced a FAIL, the build gets a bounded repair round. At each wave boundary, the loop updates Claude Code and agy and smoke-tests them before dispatch. When fixes land on main, the loop rebuilds and restarts itself at the next boot.

pillars.title: An independent second mind
pillars.claim: Built to challenge the work, not to approve it blindly.
pillars.proof: By default, a reviewer from a different model family tries to break each change before it ships. A new code-review phase between build and audit scores each change on a shared quality index of ten dimensions. It runs in shadow now. The audit keeps the block until each named defect is fixed or honestly deferred.

pillars.title: Any model. No lock-in.
pillars.claim: One routing table sends each phase to the right model.
pillars.proof: One cli_routing table in .evolve/policy.json decides every dispatch, and evolve cli-routing is its only writer. In the table that builds Evolve Loop, agy runs first, on Gemini 3.8 Flash High. Deep and top seats run Claude Opus through agy, then through Claude Code. The auditor, the tdd engineer and the code reviewer run on Claude Code only. Codex and local models through Ollama are also routable.

pillars.title: Loops that converge
pillars.claim: Built so that every loop that repeats converges or escalates.
pillars.proof: One convergence policy is built to decide the next step of every loop that repeats (ADR-0126). It runs in shadow now: no loop calls it yet. First it changes the feedback, then the strategy, then the scope. A fourth round never occurs, and a CRITICAL finding is never deferred.

pillars.title: Standards, enforced
pillars.claim: The bar is in the tools, not in a style guide.
pillars.proof: Code explains itself: the commit gate refuses a commit that adds a comment. Every code change is test-first, and mutation tests check the tests. Every landing passes a review loop with a convergence rule. The documentation moves to ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English: 21 core documents use it now, and its lint is in progress.

comparison.heading: When to use it.
rows: It plans and scopes the work
Retry until the budget is gone
Converge or escalate, never a fourth round (in shadow)
Compounds: each run teaches the next
One routing table: the best model for each phase
comparison.note: Think of the agent as the developer. Evolve Loop is the team and the process around it: the plan, the review and the discipline that make the output safe to ship.

examples.heading: From one command to full control.
examples.sub: Start with a goal. Add a flag only when you want more. Each note tells what the command does behind the scenes.

items.label: Just a goal
items.note: The advisor composes the whole pipeline: which phases run, which CLI and model run each phase, and how many cycles. It stops when the work is done.

items.label: Steer the approach
items.note: A strategy (harden · repair · innovate · balanced) changes the scope and the strictness. The phase spine stays the same, and the posture changes.

items.label: Bound the cycles
items.note: --cycles N is a hard contract: exactly N cycles, with no early stop.

items.label: Stack the levers
items.note: Compose them: a strategy, a hard cycle bound and a goal in one command. This is the full-control end of the range.

items.label: Resume
items.note: It continues a run from its last checkpoint, with the worktree and the state intact. No work is lost.

items.label: Save work in progress
items.note: It saves the uncommitted work of each dev worktree as a ref under refs/checkpoints. It does not change the branch, the index or the working tree. evolve checkpoint restore puts the work into a new or clean worktree.

items.label: Queue a backlog
items.note: evolve inbox add is the one way to file an item. The loop takes items in the order of a computed rank: weight, priority class, the items that it unblocks, recurrence, age and goal. The verbs show, list, edit, verify and withdraw curate an item, and each verb validates its change.

items.label: Route the work
items.note: It marks an item as operator-owned (route: console-manual). After that, every lane's claim refuses the item. evolve inbox route-lane reverses a false positive. Routing is plumbing, not a prompt.

items.label: Explain the routing
items.note: It prints the CLI chain of an agent from the one routing table. The verbs init, set, unset and migrate of evolve cli-routing are the only writers of the table.

items.label: Go wide
items.note: Parallel lanes, each in its own git worktree. Quota pressure shrinks the width, but never below one isolated lane and never onto your main tree.

items.label: Publish
items.note: A release pipeline that repairs itself: preflight gates, the changelog, an atomic version bump and a CI-verified publish. If the remote suite fails, the release demotes itself, so "latest" never points at a broken build.

setup.heading: Setup is one command, and it is optional
setup.note: Run it once. It finds your installed LLM CLIs and offers three presets, and one choice writes per-phase routing to .evolve/policy.json. If the project declares a cli_routing table, setup refuses, and evolve cli-routing edits the table. If you skip setup, each phase uses the defaults of its profile.

concurrency.heading: Run several loops at once.
concurrency.sub: Give each feature its own loop, and the loops run side by side. Each loop has its own git worktree and branch, and it composes the pipeline that its goal needs. The routing table picks the CLI for each phase. The loops never collide, and only green changes merge to main, one at a time.

scenarios.title: Many features at once
scenarios.note: Point a loop at each goal. The loops advance in parallel, not in a queue.

scenarios.title: Isolated by design
scenarios.note: Each loop owns a worktree and a branch: no crossed wires, no half merges.

scenarios.title: Safe, serialized merges
scenarios.note: Only green work reaches main, one merge at a time.

concurrency.noteLead: All you need is an LLM CLI subscription.
concurrency.note: Each lane runs on the CLIs that you already use, for example agy and Claude Code.

tryIt.heading: One line. See what you get.
tryIt.sub: No account. No telemetry. One static binary. The installer verifies its checksum, sets up your PATH and connects the skills to each AI CLI that you already use.
tryIt.platforms: macOS & Linux · Apple Silicon + x64 · Windows through WSL2
tryIt.verified: verified end-to-end on macOS, Debian, and Alpine

trust.label: Read install.sh before you run it

inboxLab.heading: You never stop the loop. You feed it.
inboxLab.sub: The queue is how you steer. While the loop runs, you file a JSON item with evolve inbox add. Every cycle, triage takes the top of a computed rank: weight, priority class, the items that it unblocks, recurrence, age and goal. The other items age forward, with no restart and no lost work. When an audit goes red, the retro files a lesson as a new item, and the failed item returns with its worktree. In the demo below, every third cycle fails, and the rank shows only the weight.
inboxLab.note: Real schema, in short: id, weight, title, kind and fix. A real item also has acceptance[] criteria, which the auditor enforces, and a priority_class.

presets.label: Bug
presets.title: Events sink closed while a timed-out watcher can still write
presets.fix: Close the sink only after the watcher exits; accept the fd leak on timeout.

presets.label: Feature
presets.title: evolve tokens report — per-phase usage table
presets.fix: Walk the last N cycles; rank phases by input tokens; show cache-hit ratio.

presets.label: Refactor
presets.title: Four ledger writers, one lock — merge them into a single Append
presets.fix: One typed writer behind a port; delete the three hand-rolled copies.

presets.label: Security
presets.title: Guard test passes silently for the wrong reason when HOME is unset
presets.fix: Inject the home dir; pin deny+alarm with HOME isolated.

gateLab.heading: Autonomy without shortcuts.
gateLab.sub: Bypass mode means “do not ask the operator”. It never means “skip the checks”. A floor compiled into the binary evaluates every cycle before anything ships. Change the evidence and see the verdict change.

checks.label: Independent audit says PASS
checks.evidence: audit-report.md · an adversarial auditor on Claude Code, by default a different family from the builder

checks.label: Tests written first, red observed
checks.evidence: test-report.md · the failed run before the fix

checks.label: Change is trivial, or a document
checks.evidence: the cycle classifier or deliverable_kind=document; it waives only the tdd conjunct

checks.label: Eval quality gate
checks.evidence: evolve eval quality-check: no tautological or unsatisfiable predicates

checks.label: Tree state attested
checks.evidence: tree-diff guard · SHA binding from audit to ship

gateLab.note: These are compiled Go defaults, not config that you can forget to set. The floor holds even when a model writes every prompt in the pipeline. The new code-review phase runs in shadow, so it does not gate a ship yet.

recoveryLab.heading: Failure is routed, not fatal.
recoveryLab.sub: A failure adapter classifies and routes every abnormal exit. It can retry, move the phase to the next CLI in the routing table, re-pin or reconcile. The queue survives, the evidence stays honest and the loop continues.

events.label: Audit verdict: FAIL — honest red
steps: The auditor grades the work red, and the verdict stands: a judgment phase gets no remediation
The retro classifies the failure: honest rejection, pipeline fault or operator-owned. The deterministic failure digest gives the fingerprint
A lesson and a follow-up item go back into the queue, and the worktree stays for salvage
The item returns to the queue, and the next cycle takes the top of the rank
events.outcome: A failed cycle feeds the queue. It does not stop the queue.

events.label: Gate forced FAIL over a PASS
steps: The auditor writes PASS, but a deterministic gate (for example, skills-drift) forces FAIL
One table gives each gate a failure class and a one-step remedy
The build gets a bounded repair round, with the remedy first in its brief (2 retries at most)
A FAIL from a static gate cannot halt the loop because of the prose in a retro
events.outcome: A FAIL that only gates forced gets a repair, not a halt.

events.label: Provider quota exhausted
steps: The signal center classifies exit 85 as quota exhaustion
A usage query verifies the quota and records the verdict as evidence
The CLI goes on the bench for its reset window: a fast fail, no zombie waits
The chain of the routing table sends the phase to the next CLI, and the phase completes there
events.outcome: The provider is benched. The loop is not.

events.label: agy-claude booted the wrong model
steps: Before the prompt, agy-claude waits up to 10 s for a claude-family label in the footer
No claude-family label shows, so the launch stops with exit 87
Exit 87 is a walk trigger: the seat moves to Claude Code
The deep phase completes on Claude Opus
events.outcome: The model family that runs is the family that the table asked for.

events.label: REPL boot timeout
steps: The liveness probe sees no pane output before the deadline
The bridge records a boot strike against this CLI
A relaunch with backoff; repeated strikes bench the CLI
The phase completes on the retry
events.outcome: A transient boot failure costs seconds, not cycles.

events.label: Ship binary tampered
steps: Ship refuses: the current binary ≠ the pinned SHA
A provenance check: did the loop build it from source that it shipped?
A provenance-gated auto-repin updates the pin at boot
The next cycle ships clean
events.outcome: A blocked ship and a repaired pin: trust is verified, never assumed.

events.label: Push rejected — origin moved
steps: Ship detects the diverged origin
The cycle work stays safe on its lane branch
At the batch boundary, sync-main reconciles: merge only, nothing forced
The next ship fast-forwards
events.outcome: A divergence becomes a boundary chore, not a lost cycle.

events.label: No phase artifact
steps: Runner: no report artifact before the deadline
A transient bridge error? One retry
Still absent: the runner backfills the report from the session transcript
The audit verifies the backfilled artifact again before anything ships

recoveryLab.proof: This is not hypothetical. An experiment with a new model once put several regressions into one run. None of them reached a human: the pipeline's own reviews caught each one and recovered. Within two days, the pipeline turned each one into a permanent safeguard. Runs can fail, and failures become fixes that stay.

finalCta.heading: Let the loop read the diffs you did not write.
finalCta.subhead: Open source. Apache-2.0. Works with Antigravity, Claude Code, Codex and Ollama.

footer.grounding: Grounded in reflective self-improvement and double-loop learning.
